Question: What is something you have always wanted to do but have never done?
Answer: I have always been a man of action. I have taken many bold steps in my life to realise my dreams. However, there are still several things that I always wanted to do, but have never done. 1: Girlfriend When I was in college, I wanted to have a girlfriend, as I did not wish to marry an unknown person. The competition was tough as there were hardly half a dozen girls in our batch of 300 students in IT-BHU, and none in my branch of Mechanical Engineering. However, I was too shy to approach a girl. I also did not have the guts to face rejection. So, I never had a girlfriend in my life. I finally got married arranged by my parents, just after meeting my wife once before the wedding. Now, I have been happily married for 32 years, with two daughters, both married. 2: Academic Career After I quit the IRS, I thought of becoming a Professor at a management college in India and enjoying the academic environment. I applied to more than a dozen colleges in India but did not get a single invite even for an interview. Hence, I could never teach students as a full professor, nor could I live on a beautiful campus as a professor. 3: Interaction with Foreigners I have always been fascinated by English, Germans, and Americans, who have produced so many great scientists, philosophers, artists, writers and musicians. So, when I recently visited Munich (Germany) and stayed with my children for around 75 days, I thought of befriending some local German people and understanding their culture and beliefs. Almost everyone around was a German, but I could never approach and befriend them. 4: Lectures and Seminars I wanted to organise seminars and lecture people to share my thoughts and interact with the live audience. However, organising an event is too much of a hassle and I find it too difficult, especially ensuring that a decent number of people attend the event. Hence, I could never do such an event. 5: Living in a Beautiful Place I often dream of living like an author in a beautiful place amid nature to be inspired. I had stayed in such places for a couple of days, but I wished to stay there for a few weeks or months, taking a walk in the morning and evening, sitting below a tree, gazing at the mountains. However, whenever I proposed a long stay to my wife, she rejected it, “You will be busy with your computer, what will I do?” I have never stayed alone, nor can I imagine myself staying alone, so this wish is also yet to be realised. I hope that one day, I will develop enough courage to fulfil these dreams, except, of course, having a girlfriend, for which time has passed, and I would not do any misadventure at this age. Question: Can you describe the experience of being an IAS or IRS officer in India? Is there a sense of happiness and satisfaction in this role?
Answer: I have been an IRS officer for 25 years (1991–2016). My experience as an IRS officer has been quite good. The reasons are as follows. As an IRS officer of Indirect Taxes (Customs, GST & Narcotics), you get exposure as a tax officer, adjudicator, police officer (Narcotics and Anti-smuggling) and as educator and trainer (in Academies). Here is my old picture in uniform as a Deputy Commissioner of Customs and Central Excise. I was happy and proud to be an IRS officer, and I enjoyed great satisfaction during my career as an IRS officer. In civil services, IAS is still the best service, as you get exposure to almost every department of the state and central government. Further, you also get the best facilities and perks, and the fastest promotion as an IAS officer. However, there are no free lunches in the world. As an IAS officer, you have to face political interference, frequent transfers, long working hours and poor work-life balance. However, professional satisfaction and recognition in IAS are the best among all civil services. Hence, if you join either IAS or IRS, you are likely to be happy and satisfied, provided you learn to value what you have rather than lamenting on the negative aspect of your service by focusing your mind on what you lack.

Question: What is the difference between Europe and India?
Answer: In Germany, there are agreed-upon quiet hours (Ruhezeit), usually from 10 pm to 6 am on weekdays, and the entire day on Sundays. Ruhezeit also applies during public holidays for the entire day. The rule of thumb is that you can make noise up to normal room volume (up to 50 decibels), but anything louder is a no-no. For example, during Ruhezeit, you can’t use a vacuum, wash your car, drill, or mow your lawn.[1] If you violate the Ruhezeit, your neighbour can call police, and you may end up paying a huge fine for violating the law. I was in Germany, Munich, for 75 days last year and I did not see anyone violating the law. My daughter and son-in-law are in Munich for more than 5 years and they also have not come across any violation. They will not use even the mixie or vacuum on silent hours, lest someone call the police. There are also laws of quiet hours in India. The Government of Uttar Pradesh order prohibits the use of loudspeakers after 10 PM and before 6 AM. These guidelines are issued in compliance with the directions of the Hon'ble High Court Lucknow Bench and for implementation of Noice Pollution Control Act as per the notifications issued by Govt. of India.[2] These directions are often prominently displayed in the hotels and the important venues. I have taken this picture when I recently attended a marriage function in Lucknow, where you see the notice by police on the back. Unfortunately, despite the clear-cut direction of High Court, the Government of India and the state government, hardly anyone bothers about observing them. Last month, near to my place, a DJ was playing at full volume at a marriage function and we could not sleep. So I complaint twice about emergency no 112, but nothing happened and the DJ stopped only at 1.00 AM, as per their wish. In the morning, I took a picture of the venue and posted it on my twitter account tagging Lucknow police. It was informed by Lucknow police that they have issued the direction to local police station. However, the DJ still plays late in night, Now, if you think that DJ is the main problem, you are wrong. They at least are over in couple of hours. Just two weeks ago, there was an Akhand Ramayan using a loudspeaker very near to my house, which you know continues for 24 hours. When the loudspeaker volume did not come down after even 11 PM, I went personally to the venue and requested them to lower the volume or switch of the loudspeaker. However, there was no effect. Then I called on 112 twice in the night, but the Akhand Ramayan continued with full volume throughout the night, and we could not sleep for a minute. Similarly, just last week, there was a Jagrata near our place and the bhajans continued throughout the night. I called 112 again, and the police also came, but still, the Jagrata continued throughout the night and we could not sleep again. I am not against these religious functions, but the people must comply with the law and switch off the loudspeaker at least at night. However, who cares about humans when you are trying to get the blessing of God and you want to reach Him/Her through the loudspeaker? To be fair, Lucknow police managed to twice shut down the DJ, when it was played in a private party, but could not act on marriage functions and religious functions. I discussed the matter with fellow residents and they said that it is futile to complain to stop the loudspeakers on religious events like Akhand Path or Jagrata, since police never act on such occasions. I better get used to live with the reality. There is a huge difference between India and European countries. In Europe, laws are observed, while in India, laws are defied. The worst thing is that people become so insensitive to their neighbours that they don’t care that because of their actions so many other people are facing inconvenience. Many students were writing their Board’s examinations or preparing for competitions, but these people are unconcerned about them in their quest to get the blessing of God and earn punya. The government often does not act on religious functions because these religious people are their vote banks, and they can’t afford to lose them. When religion becomes the focus of politics, religious people become above the law, as they know that the government will not act against them. The trend is continuously increasing, as religion is now used more and more in politics. In a civilised world, people obey the laws and care for society, but hardly these things matter in India. While India aspires to become a developed nation, the country is moving more toward the medieval period. We need to do a lot of introspection and decide which direction we wish to go and in which direction, we are actually going.

Question: As an Indian, what worries you the most about India and its people?
Answer: I was reading the morning newspaper ‘The Times of India’ today, where I came across the following news item KVT witnesses 5 lakh devotees on Sun (17th March 2024), a new record for a normal day. The newspaper further states. Over five lakh devotees (half a Million) visited Kashi Vishwanath Dham on Sunday — a fresh record for any day other than the festive or special occasions like Mahashivratri, Mondays of Shrawan and New Year. The average footfall of normal days of temple has gone above 1.50 lakh per day after Jan 31,” ..According to temple authorities, before the opening of KV Dham the average footfall per day at temple ranged around 20,000 and on special occasions like Mahashivratri it used to witness over 2.50 lakh devotees.[1] (Above File photo of the crowd of devotees at KV temple in Shravan Month.[2]) It is evident that the number of visitors in KV Dham has gone up to 7–8 times in just three years, and the same appears to be the case of most religious places in India. The Kumbh Mela 2019 had seen the largest religious and spiritual mass gatherings on the Earth, as around 240 million pilgrims participated during the Mela. [3] The upcoming Maha Kumbh 2025 in Prayagraj is expected to attract around 40 crore (400 Million) visitors starting on January 13, 2025. [4] I had the opportunity to visit many cities in Europe in countries like Germany, Switzerland, Italy, and Austria, in 2023, and almost every city in Europe is full of churches. However, I did not find any crowd at all in these churches. Most of these churches are totally empty, and the visitors are mostly tourists who are non-Christian, who visit these places as tourist spots, and visitors often have to pay an entrance fee, as the churches can’t maintain themselves with charity alone. I took the following picture before the ‘The Berlin Cathedral’, the most beautiful church in the city. There was no crowd at all. We paid a 20 euro fee to go inside the church. What really worries me about India and the Indian people is the surge of devotion and visits to religious places in recent years. Where are we going? I feel sorry for people who take so much pain, and spend so much money and time to visit temples with such high hopes from God to transform their lives, rather than taking responsibility for their lives and improving them with better education and hard work. While the world is becoming more rational in modern times by developing scientific temper and losing their faith in God, India is moving in just the opposite direction, where the faith of people in God is increasing exponentially, thanks to our politicians who have made religion as the main agenda for the political battle. Religious fundamentalism in India is increasing with every passing day, while the developed world is slowly moving away from the religious way of life by developing rational thinking and scientific temper. I feel scared of the future of India as we are going backwards towards the past, instead of progressing towards development and prosperity.

Question: Why do some people believe that others have no right to criticize their opinions and beliefs? Is it important to respect everyone's opinion as long as it doesn't harm anyone else?
Answer: I have written more than 5700 answers on Quora and received 284316 comments. The latest screenshots of my contents are as follows. While most of the people who like my answer simply upvotes them, those who dislike me often criticize my answers. By conservative estimates, I must have got at least around 25% criticism of my answers or around 50,000 negative comments. I expect negative comments, particularly when I write answers on political and religious subjects, and use criticism to understand the other side of the story, which I could not see when I wrote my answers. I take every criticism seriously and use them to improve my writing. Sometimes, when I find the criticism accurate, I edit my answer immediately. However, some criticism gets too personal and they hit below the belt. I am not perfect, but that does not give anyone a right to make a personal comment or allegations like, Some comments use such abusive words that I can’t even write them here. In some comments, I have even got the threat of life. I have even got abusive emails and threatening phone calls from people who felt offended by my answers. No one has the right to make personal allegations or abuse a writer to share his or her views. Let us understand that the world has grown only because some people showed the courage to defy popular beliefs, and spoke the truth despite public criticism. Imagine if we did not have people like Socrates, Buddha, Jesus Christ, Mahavir Jain, Galileo, Mahanta Gandhi, Abraham Lincoln, Nelson Mandela or Martin Luther King Junior, who fought for truth and justice risking their lives. I am certainly nowhere near them, but I try to show the other perspective of reality, which may not be popular but also contains a grain of truth because I believe that to make a sound decision, we must always hear both sides of the story. Hearing all sides is a very important part of natural justice also. Ultimately, it is you, who will decide what is right and wrong, after hearing all sides of the story. My thoughts echo with Paulo Coelho, “I write from my soul. This is the reason that critics don't hurt me, because it is me. If it was not me, if I was pretending to be someone else, then this could unbalance my world, but I know who I am.” Please criticise me as much as you want, but don’t get personal and make unsubstantiated allegations against me. It takes a lot of courage to write anything on a public platform like Quora and frankly express your views. India is a country which believes in the assimilation of culture and unity in diversity. Let us learn from each other to become the best version of ourselves rather than hating people having different opinions and hitting them below the belt to threaten and punish them for sharing their views.

Question: Why is it so difficult for most people to develop the resolve to take the path less traveled?
Answer: We humans are social animals and it is scary to travel on a path where you can’t see any person travelling with you. Most people prefer to live their lives by following the herd because they feel safe with them. Hence, most people study hard during their younger days, get a job, get married, have kids, take care of their responsibilities, provide them with a good education, get them married and then spend time with their grandchildren. This conventional path is the easiest and safest. For instance, in FY 23, 8.12 million new jobs were created by Indian companies, including 2.06 million jobs in IT sector alone. [1] So, if you have followed the common path by doing engineering, particularly in computer science and IT, and you stand even at the 2 millions position in India, you can hope to get a job and earn a decent living. Now, think about the people who are following the path less travelled, and choose to become writers, actors, artists, musicians, singers, cricketers or other sportspersons etc. The possibilities of success and earning a decent income in the less-travelled path is very small. You are practically a nobody in any creative field unless you are in the top 0.1%. For instance, In the creative field, it is the winner takes all, and if you don’t stand in the top 0.1%, you are a failure. Thus the failure rate is very high, more than 99%. The best example is Quora itself, which has over 400 million monthly active users.[3] Even if 10% of them are writers, there are at least 40 Million writers on Quora. However, hardly a few thousand writers on Quora may be getting decent views and upvotes. How disappointed do you feel when no one recognises and appreciates your work, even if its quality may be better than the so-called top writers on Quora? The same thing happens when you write a book with years of effort and can’t sell even a few hundred copies of the book to cover even the printing cost. It is true that a small percentage of people who travel on the path-less-travelled discover new territories and become world-famous, but most people get lost on this path. The following cartoon tells the story of most people who walk on the path less travelled.[4] Jerry Seinfeld said it aptly, “Sometimes the road less traveled is less traveled for a reason”. Hence, instead of choosing the road less travelled based on anecdotal evidence and emotions, find out the reasons why fewer people are travelling on a particular path. Once you understand the real reasons for people avoiding the path-less-travelled, prepare yourself well to face the challenges and pain of your new venture, and make a proper strategy to achieve success in your chosen path. Scott Peck, author of the best-selling book The Road Less Traveled, said this wisely, “Life is difficult. This is a great truth, one of the greatest truths. It is a great truth because once we truly see this truth, we transcend it. Once we truly know that life is difficult, once we truly understand and accept it, then life is no longer difficult. Because once it is accepted, the fact that life is difficult no longer matters”. Source

Question: How has the Narendra Modi government reduced corruption in India?
Answer: It is a myth that corruption is reducing under the Modi government. As a matter of fact, corruption has continuously increased since the Modi government came to power in 2014. It is evident from the report of German-based Transparency International, an international agency to assess corruption in different countries in the world, that India’s ranking is getting worse after 2015. While India was continuously improving its ranking before 2014–2015 and rose from ranking 94 to 76, since 2015, it has been decreasing and now in 2023, it is 93. [1] Similarly, India is the worst Asian country according to the citizen survey of corruption in India and select Asian countries according to a report in 2020 where 39% of the citizens accepted to have paid bribes to government officers, worse than any other Asian country surveyed. [2] What the Modi government has done is to make the anti-corruption agencies powerless by amending Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act in 2018 so that now the officers of CBI or other agencies can’t even start corruption cases against the government employees without the permission of the Government.[3] Further, governments are now appointing only loyal officers, who, instead of following the law books, would never make any case against the government, and only target the opposition. As a result, you don’t hear cases of corruption booked against government officers and ministers nowadays, though corruption is increasing every year under the present regime. However, most people in India have become so blind due to their faith, that they will ignore every evidence against their Supreme leader whom they consider nothing less than God’s incarnation in Kaliyoga.

Question: I've begged, prayed, whispered and screamed for God's guidance and have felt nothing? What am I doing wrong?
Answer: Your question reminds me of a very famous story about God trying to help a believer. A fellow was stuck on his rooftop in a flood. He was praying to God for help. Soon a man in a rowboat came by and the fellow shouted to the man on the roof, “Jump in, I can save you.” The stranded fellow shouted back, “No, it’s OK, I’m praying to God and he is going to save me.” So the rowboat went on. Then a motorboat came by. “The fellow in the motorboat shouted, “Jump in, I can save you.” To this the stranded man said, “No thanks, I’m praying to God and he is going to save me. I have faith.” So the motorboat went on. Then a helicopter came by and the pilot shouted down, “Grab this rope and I will lift you to safety.” To this the stranded man again replied, “No thanks, I’m praying to God and he is going to save me. I have faith.” So the helicopter reluctantly flew away. Soon the water rose above the rooftop and the man drowned. He went to Heaven. He finally got his chance to discuss this whole situation with God, at which point he exclaimed, “I had faith in you but you didn’t save me, you let me drown. I don’t understand why!” To this God replied, “I sent you a rowboat and a motorboat and a helicopter, what more did you expect?”[1] This story is often used to convince people that when they are in difficult situations, God help them by sending different people. Hence, if in your difficult time, someone helps you, it is due to God and you should be grateful to God for His help. Now, first of all, this story is purely a figment of imagination, because no person would come back to this world after having a conversation with God to share his story with people. Assuming there is some truth in the story, what would have been the reply of God, if a believer who died in the following way asked the same question to God, “I had faith in you but you didn’t save me, you let me drown. I don’t understand why!” Do you expect God to accept that He sent these murderous people to kill you? Question: Why should I help others? If I don't, what will be the consequences?
Answer: When I was young, we used to spend our summer vacations in our native village in Raibereli. In those days, almost all marriages used to take place in the summer because it is cheaper to arrange a marriage in the summer than in the winter when you have to arrange for warm clothes, quilts etc. Marriage in the village in those days used to be celebrated like a festival. Instead of hotels, the Barat (marriage party) used to stay in gardens under lush green trees. In place of procuring bedding and utensils from the tent house, we used to borrow them from our relatives and other villagers. There would be no hired cooks or waiters in the marriage. All the members of the clan would be participating in the preparation of the food. While men would be cutting and chopping the vegetables, women folks would prepare the chapatis (bread) and purées (fried bread). Instead of waiters, the family members and the villagers would be serving the food themselves to the guests. The cost of arranging marriage was thus quite low as all services were free. However, marriages happen in different ways in cities, and things have changed even in the villages. My daughters got married a few years ago. We booked the hotel, caterers, cars etc. Since we were staying in a different city, we flew to the city for a marriage function just two days before. Neither we nor the guests had any work to do since all preparations were done by the hotel staff and caterers. They had to only dress up and get ready to participate in various functions of the marriage and do the necessary rituals. Almost all guests departed the next day of marriage and we also left the place within two days of marriage. The effort required for the arrangement of the marriage of my daughter was much lesser compared to what used to take place in the village, and it was much superior. However, arranging marriage in a hotel costs many times more money than the marriages organized in the village. The arrangement of marriage in a village appears quite romantic, beautiful, and economical. However, now even in the villages, the marriage functions are not arranged in the old way as the economic conditions of people have improved. There are no free lunches in the world and certainly, there are hidden costs and obligations when we receive help from someone for free. When you accept the help of the family and society members, you bound yourself with the obligation to provide free services whenever marriage takes place in their families. If you fail to fulfil your obligation, you will suffer criticism, condemnation and exclusion from the society. On the other side, when you make all the arrangements using professionals, you pay the market rates for the services and there is no further obligation from either side. There is no need to help other people if you don’t need their help. Helping random people shall not help you in the time of your need. Help those, like family, friends, close relatives, and neighbours, who may help you back at the time of your need. When you help others selflessly, you also expect selfless help from other, which does not usually come in real life. When your life depends on the help of others, you feel helpless, angry and frustrated when help does not come. It is good to be kind and helpful to people in their time of need, but it is not an obligation on you unless you have taken help from them or hope to take their help in future. You must first help yourself by earning and saving enough money so that when the time comes, rather than seeking any help from anyone, you can pay for all the services that you need from people, and live a good life. You must always help those who have helped you in past. You may help the strangers only when you feel they need it and they are also ready to help themselves. It is often said that even God help those who help themselves. Source of pictures: Google Images

Question: Why would we rather believe lies which make us comfortable than truth that makes us feel unpleasant?
Answer: I have fairly good experience of life and people and I have not seen or known any person who can deliberately believe a lie. A person can believe a lie, only when he or she thinks that it is true. Our mind is simply incapable of believing anything which it knows is a lie. Similarly, our mind is also incapable of disbelieving anything which it knows as a truth. However, it is also a fact that most people believe in lies rather than truth. Mark Twain once said, “A lie can travel halfway around the world while the truth is still putting on its shoes.” A study by three MIT scholars has found that false news spreads more rapidly on the social network Twitter than real news does — and by a substantial margin. For instance, Let us investigate why most people believe in falsehood when their mind is designed to believe nothing but the truth We know that scientists have discovered that the human brain can be divided into two halves with clearly divided functions as shown in the following diagram.[2] We can see very easily that all right-brain activities are natural. While the right brain can be sharpened and made more powerful with increased left-brain activity, even left to itself, as emotional brain are perfectly capable of functioning on their own. Hence, even an illiterate person has emotions and he can enjoy emotional movies and songs. Similarly, even a young child’s right-brain is duly functional and is quite creative, imaginative and artistic. He/She is also highly emotional and is capable of expressing himself through non-verbal signals. However, our left-side (rational) brain is not functional on its own and must be developed by None of the left-brain activities is inborn or natural, and we have to acquire them with great effort. Imagine a person whose left (rational) brain is totally blank because the person has not learned anything in life, or has no idea of the subject before him. He/she has no option, but to rely on the emotional brain alone to make judgments and believe anything based on emotions, intuition and imagination. Emotional decisions are governed by our feelings: Hence, when a person is ignorant of the information presented to him, he will believe it to be true if it feels good and reject it if it feels bad. Since lies are designed specially to please people, hence, an ignorant person will always prefer comfortable lies and reject the truth if that is unpleasant. To appreciate and know the truth, you have to make the left or rational brain more powerful by acquiring knowledge and learning the skill to use arguments, logic and analysis, which needs lots of hard work, which most people find difficult and unpleasant. Since most people are not willing to devote time to learning the truth, they reject the unpleasant truth and believe in the comfortable lies. However, believing in lies does not make lie a truth, not believing a truth makes it false. You cheat only yourself by believing in lies and ignoring the truth. It may be wise to remember the words of Sri Chinmoy Ignorance is an enemy, even to its owner. Knowledge is a friend, even to its hater. Ignorance hates knowledge because it is too pure. Knowledge fears ignorance because it is too sure.

Question: What painful experience taught you the biggest lesson in life?
Answer: There is one famous Aesop’s Fable that I read when I was a kid. Once upon a time, lived a father and his son. One day, they went to the market with their donkey. While walking in the forest, they came across a couple. When the husband saw neither son nor father rode a donkey, he said, “You have a donkey. Why don’t you ride it?” They agreed with this idea and the son was seated on the donkey. After a while, they came across a man. The man said, “What a disrespectful son! He is riding while his father is walking.” Then the boy got down and father seated on the donkey. They continued for a while and came across a woman. The woman said, “Poor boy! Lazy father doesn’t let him ride.” Both father and son sat on a donkey and continued travelling. Then they came across another couple. They said, “What a cruel people. They both are riding poor donkey. They will kill it.” Father and son heard this and got down. They began to carry donkey on their back. Seeing this, the couple started laughing loudly. The donkey was scared of the laughter and broke free.[1] The teacher then told us the morals of the story, which are The story, however, presents before us a great dilemma. We have learned since our childhood that it is good to be appreciated and bad to be criticised. Hence, we always try to do what please everyone and we also avoid doing actions which may be criticised by others. However, this story tells us that it is impossible to please everyone and avoid criticism. So, what should we do? When I started writing on Quora in 2015, I hardly had any followers. At that time, my greatest concern was that no one was reading my post. I would visit my posts several times a day and would feel delighted if I got an upvote. My pleasure would know no limit if I find some comments on my post. I will happily reply to the comments and even thank the people who followed me. Gradually, I was getting popular, particularly after I started writing answers on civil services and political issues. Many of my answers got even a million views and hundreds of comments. Unfortunately, all comments were not positive and complimentary. Many comments were highly critical of my answer, and full of hate messages and even personal threats. Initially, I tried to reason with my critics and explain to them my viewpoint. However, the more I defended myself, the more I was trolled. I learned the lessons of Aesop’s Fable in a very hard way that you can’t please everyone and there is no way to avoid criticism, particularly if you are popular or important. You are free of criticism only if you are a nobody, as they say, ‘No one kicks a dead dog’. I then learned to ignore the trolls, or block and report them, if they become personal and abusive. The Aesops Fable are, however, moresuitable to children, whose mind is not ripe to understand the complexity of life. However, it would be foolish to keep believing one line moral message of the story as a grown up person, who must be be able to understand all sides of the story, critically analyse the issue and understand the deeper message from such stories. The most valuable lesson that I learned from my painful experience is that appreciation and criticism always come together. Most of us fail to achieve our full potential in life, because we fear criticism and do everything to avoid being criticised. As a result, we don’t make decisions, or avoid sharing our views on controversial topics. The greatest mistake that we make in life is that we fail to value the appreciation that comes with our work because our mind is focused more on criticism. What Aesop’s Fable does not tell you is the appreciation the father and son would have got when they are travelling with the donkey, as their minds are focused only on criticism. Understanding this missing perspective is the key to leading a happy and successful life. Let me explain how many people would have appreciated the father and son in each case. How lucky are they to have a donkey to ride, while we have to walk all the way? (When both were riding the lonely) What a great son the boy is. He chose to walk so that his old father could ride the donkey. (When the father was riding the donkey) What a loving father the man is to walk so that the son can travel in comfort. I wish my father was also as loving. (When the son was riding) What a nice human being the father and son are. They choose to walk rather than ride on the old donkey. (When both were walking.) Hence, you must learn to focus more on the appreciation of the people rather than the critics to achieve a happy and successful life. Learned to show your spine and take a stand on what you think is right. Don’t commit the foolishness of carrying the donkey on your shoulders to avoid criticism, and become a laughing stock. It is well said in Hindi “Hanthi chale bajar, Kutte bhoke Hazar” (Elephants walk in the market, while a thousand dogs are barking) Winston Churchill, one of the most loved as well criticised people of the twentieth century, wisely said “You have enemies? Good. That means you've stood up for something, sometime in your life.” With great difficulty and pain, I have learned to accept criticism as part of life, which may be painful, but without it, you can never do anything worthwhile in life or achieve success and appreciation in the world.

Question: Is the distance to the Sun from the Earth found in the Hanuman Chalisa? How did Tulsidas know this?
Answer: It is a great misconception that Tulsidas knew the exact distance between the Sun and Earth. Many people use the following Doha of Hanuman Chalisa as proof. जुग सहस्र जोजन पर भानू। लील्यो ताहि मधुर फल जानू॥ 18 They derive the following numbers for calculating the distance, 1 Juga =12000 years, 1 Sahastra =1000 , 1 Jojana (Yojan)=8 miles Therefore, the distance between the sun and the earth is = 12000 *1000 * 8 = 96,000,000 miles, which is quite close to the actual distance between the sun and the earth i.e. 98 Million miles. However, this method is based on the assumption that by the word Juga, Tulsidas meant a number which is equivalent to 12000. However, this assumption is incorrect. In reality, Tusidas has used the word Jug (जुग ) at least 50 times in his most popular book RamcharitMans, and the meaning of the word Jug is as follows. The most authentic source of Hindu scriptures is considered to be Gita Press, which has been awarded the prestigious Gandhi Peace Prize 2021 by the Government of India. [1] This is the book of Ramcharitmanas published by Gita Press.[2] For example, in the following Dohas from Ramcharitamanas, Jug means 2, Similarly in the following Dohas, Jug means a very long time as a metaphor, as an Atishyoki Alankar. Nowhere, does Tuslidas mean that the meaning of Jug is the number 12000? Hence, the meaning of Jug in Doha of Hanuman Chalisa here is not 12000, but 2. With this calculation, the estimation of the distance between Earth and the sun by Tulsidas comes to 2000 Yojan or 2x1000x8=16,000 Miles only, while the real distance is 98,000,000 Miles. Even Gita Press's published translation states that the distance between the sun and the earth is 16,000 miles, though they have taken different values of Jug(4) and Yojana (4 miles). Hence, it is evident that Tuslidas did not have a correct idea about the distance between Earth and the sun, and the calculation method used by the people is an extrapolation and an afterthought. Let us use our common sense and understand that Tulsidas was a poet and not a scientist to have known this exact distance. It is absurd to believe that he could know the distance between the earth and the sun by intuition or by divine knowledge even before scientists could measure it. Religious books are good sources of devotion and moral values, but they must not be used for scientific interpretations. You are welcome to provide sound arguments, if you disagree with my post. PS: If you find my arguments reasonable, forward/share this post with those who still believe that the distance between the sun and earth is written in Hanuman Chalisa.

Question: What impact do lavish pre-wedding celebrations like Anant Ambani's have on society's perception of wealth and extravagance?

Question: If you do something that you know it's wrong, but then confess and try to make amends, but the other person rejects your apology and blows you off, what should you do then?
Answer: The Chinese philosopher Lao Tzu once said, “Watch your thoughts, they become your words; watch your words, they become your actions; watch your actions, they become your habits; watch your habits, they become your character; watch your character, it becomes your destiny.” We can represent this wisdom in the form of the following diagram. In short, our thoughts decide our destiny. It is important to understand that no one does good or bad things accidentally. We do good things when we are good inside and bad things when we are inherently bad. If you are caught doing the wrong thing, like cheating on your spouse or telling lies, you lose your credibility with all the people who trust you. And it is difficult to gain trust once you lose it. A person who knows what is right and yet fails to perform the right action is weak in character and untrustworthy. Hence, our life experience suggests that if you forgive him, he will never learn his lessons and repeat the same actions again, with more caution and secrecy so that he is not caught again. He also knows now that even if he is caught again in the wrong act, he will be forgiven. Hence, people find it difficult to forgive when they catch their loved ones cheating on them and doing wrong things. Apology is not a matter of right but at the discretion of the person who is wronged by you. You can be forgiven only when the person believes that you have realised your mistakes and changed yourself to become a trustworthy person. Hence, the best way to seek forgiveness from people is not by words but by action. If you really change yourself and become a good person discarding all the bad habits, people will see the difference and they may forgive you for your past mistakes. Your mistakes may be forgiven, but will never be forgotten. Please read this Aesop’s Fable. A Countryman’s son by accident trod upon a Serpent’s tail, which turned and bit him so that he died. The father in a rage got his axe, and pursuing the Serpent, cut off part of its tail. So the Serpent in revenge began stinging several of the Farmer’s cattle and caused him severe loss. The Farmer thought it best to make it up with the Serpent, and brought food and honey to the mouth of its lair, and said to it: “Let’s forget and forgive; perhaps you were right to punish my son, and take vengeance on my cattle, but surely I was right in trying to revenge him; now that we are both satisfied why should not we be friends again?” “No, no,” said the Serpent; “take away your gifts; you can never forget the death of your son, nor I the loss of my tail.” Moral of the story: Injuries may be forgiven, but not forgotten.[1] The poet Rahimdas has beautifully said, Rahiman dhaga prem ka, mat todo chatkaya, Tute se phir na jude, jude ganth pad jaya. English translation Don't snap the delicate thread of love between people. If it breaks once, it cannot be mended. Even if you mend it there will be a knot in it. Hence, the best thing is to never do wrong things deliberately and break the hearts of your loved ones, because if your action hurts someone you love, you can never regain the same love again.

Question: Can reading books like the Bhagavad Gita get real knowledge?
Answer: Bhagwat Gita can viewed as a religious book of Hindus or a book of Indian philosophy. If you consider Gita as a religious book, everything written in the book is the word of God and you can’t question a word of it, at least if you are a Hindu. However, if you consider Gita as a philosophical text, you may agree or disagree with the knowledge contained in Gita. Let me share my views on some controversial aspect of the philosophy of Gita. 1: You have a right to perform your prescribed duties, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions. Never consider yourself to be the cause of the results of your activities, nor be attached to inaction. (BG 2.47) My view: I disagree. Our duties and rights are connected with each other. When you do your duty, you expect results. I don’t see how anyone can perform his duties if he is told that you are not entitled to the fruit. In the real world, only the result matters. Even the battle of Mahabhartha was for defeating the Kauravas. Hence, you must plan your actions in such a way that you get the results you desire. 2: Having abandoned all duties (Dharmas) take refuge in Me alone. I will liberate you from all sins. Do not grieve. (BG 18.66) My view: This goes against the karma principle. You have to pay the price for all your sinful karma. This promise can be widely misused by criminals, who are assured of liberation even after all their evil deeds. 3: Brahmanas, ksatriyas, vaisyas and sudras are distinguished by their qualities of work, O chastiser of the enemy, in accordance with the modes of nature. Peacefulness, self-control, austerity, purity, tolerance, honesty, wisdom, knowledge, and religiousness-these are the qualities by which the brahmanas work. Heroism, power, determination, resourcefulness, courage in battle, generosity, and leadership are the qualities of work for the ksatriyas. Farming, cattle raising and business are the qualities of work for the vaisyas, and for the sudras there is labor and service to others. (BG 18: 41–44)[1] My view: The concept of caste is outdated. Though some people may claim that caste is not due to birth, but to nature; in reality caste has always by birth alone in Hinduism. Even in the period of Mahabharata, Karna was always addressed as Suta Putra, in a derogatory manner as he was thought to be born in a Sudra family. He was also denied Brahmavidhya because he was neither a Brahmin nor a Kshatriya (Refer to edit). Even in the modern time, you can change your religion, but not your caste according to present Indian laws. 4: For those who take refuge in Me, Ο Pārtha, though they be of sinful birth— women, vaiśyas, and śudras— even they attain the Supreme Goal. How much more, then, if they be holy brāhmins or royal seers devoted to God! Having come into this transitory, joyless world, worship Me. (BG 9: 32–33)[2] My view: This sloka clearly subordinates the women, vaishyas, and Sudras below Brahmins, and call their birth sinful, which is not right in my opinion. Women surely are equal to men, and the concept of caste is manmade, not divine. I can point out many such instances of Gita, where I don’t agree with Gita. I know that the people who consider Gita as the ultimate philosophy and the words of God would never agree with me. However, the reality is that Gita was written several thousands years ago, and the societies have undergone tremendous change since then. Many teachings that were good for the societies that existed two thousand years ago are no more good for modern times. I have learned many good things from Gita. Gita is certainly a great book which teaches us the principle of selfless karma and motivates us to fight against injustice, but its philosophy is not infallible. We must therefore learn only the right lessons from Gita and discard those teachings which have become outdated in the modern context. Question: Life without suffering is not worth living. Do you agree?
Answer: Our natural tendency is to live a comfortable life, and avoid all types of pain. A comfortable life is pleasant, but it also makes people complacent and stunts their growth. It is wisely said, “A comfort zone is a beautiful place – but nothing ever grows there.” If you wish to give meaning to your life and make it worth living, you have to come out of your comfort zone and struggle for the betterment of the world. No person can ever become great without suffering. The list of great men who not only suffered tremendous pain in their lives, but even have to sacrifice their life for the cause is endless. Even today, we find so many wrong things happening in the world. However, we don’t fight against the evil forces because we want to lead an easy life and don’t want to suffer in life. Even if you get a good job by becoming a top civil servant, minister, or a manager, you won’t be able to make your life worth living unless you are willing to suffer. If you chose to create new product and become an entrepreneur, be ready to suffer in life. Many people can become great artists, scientists, singers, musicians, writers, but they never fulfill their dreams because they don’t want to suffer in life, and they instead choose a path which is convenient and easy to walk. It reminds me the beautiful poem of Robert Frost “The Road Not Taken” Two roads diverged in a yellow wood, And sorry I could not travel both ….. I took the one less traveled by, And that has made all the difference. The path of suffering is the road less travelled, which makes all the diference by giving meaning to our lives and make it worth living. .

Question: Is it morally justifiable for billionaires to have such vast amounts of wealth while others struggle to survive? What reasons do they give for their immense wealth?
Answer: It is common to see even the commonest person in India using a mobile phone and surfing various social media channels, making video calls to his friends and family, and learning many useful things from the internet. Some of you may remember that around eight years ago, till 2016, mobile data was so expensive in India that even rich people could not afford to surf the internet on mobile. Before Reliance launched Jio in India, customers were paying about Rs 350 for 1 GB of data. The result of Jio’s war on data prices brought the cost of 1 GB to around just Rs 13. The price of data thus fell by about 95% in 6 years, and calling became almost free which made mobile phones accessible to everyone in India.[1] Yes, Mr Mukesh Ambani, the CMD of Reliance Industries indeed has a net worth of $112.1 billion according to Forbes as of February 2024, and he is the richest person in Asia and 11th richest in the world.[2] However, let us also appreciate that he became wealthy by making a positive contribution to society and benefiting the common man through his products. If you look at any billionaire in the world, you will find that almost all of them have created a product that has improved the quality of life of people in society.[3] You don’t become rich because you wish to become rich, because that is what almost everyone desires. You become wealthy only when you contribute to the betterment of the lives of people by producing better products at cheaper prices. The world would not have been as good as it is today without their contribution. The richest people in the world also make a direct contribution to the development of the nation in multiple ways. A country is thus better developed if it provides a suitable environment for the people to realise their full potential and create wealth for themselves and the nation. Confucius, the Chinese teacher and philosopher, said this more than two thousand years ago, “In a country well governed, poverty is something to be ashamed of. In a country badly governed, wealth is something to be ashamed of.” Hence, if a person has become a billionaire following legal means in a country, he has done a great service to the nation and the world, and his actions are not only morally justifiable but morally commendable. Let more such billionaires flourish in all parts of the world, and make the world a better place for humanity. Source of picture: Google Images

Question: What are the most effective learning techniques you have experienced so far?
Answer: Let me share with you some of the techniques that I use in my life to help you make your learning easier and lasting. 1: Multiple Reading You must have noticed that when we paint our house, we don’t spend all the paint in a single coating. Instead, we apply multiple coatings. First, we apply a coat and allow it to dry and then apply the second and sometimes the third coat. In the same way, instead of reading the book once, read it multiple times. Let the first reading be just a casual reading and allow knowledge of the first reading to sink into the mind. Then after a while, make the second reading and so on. You can get better results, within the same total time. 2: Make Notes I have the habit of making notes whenever I read. Sometimes, I just highlight or underline the important text. When we are just reading something, our mind is likely to wonder. However, if side by side, we are also making notes or highlighting, it will be more focussed and our grasp will be better. Moreover, while revising, you don’t have to read the whole thing, but just focus on the notes/highlights. 3: Practice It is said that practice makes a man perfect. When you learn something, try to put into practice the knowledge in some way. In academic learning, you can solve the problems at the end of each chapter. However, when you are learning philosophy, self-help techniques or any principle, try to practice it in your life as much as you can. This will make the knowledge stick to your mind. 4: Discuss and Teach Knowledge is a wealth that multiplies by sharing. Hence, if you can share the knowledge with others by teaching or discussion, the concept will become more clear to you. You also learn about ignorance or lack of clarity during discussion and then you go back and refresh your concept. 5: Remove the Bottleneck When we learn about any subject, some topics are easy while others are difficult. We have the tendency to ignore the tough topics and focus on the easy ones. However, those difficult topics become our bottleneck of learning, and they keep bothering us all the time. Instead, you must spend considerable time mastering the difficult topics, even if it means multiple revisions or even consulting your teacher or parents. When you take care of the bottleneck, your journey becomes smooth. 6: Manage Energy Level Our energy level is not the same all the time. We are usually fresh in the morning and after siesta, but get tired before lunch, and at the end of the day. In order to get the best result, you must take the toughest topics/subjects when your mind is fresh, while taking the easy topics when your energy levels are low. Moreover, try to maintain a high energy level by taking regular breaks during studies, at least after every hour. During the breaks, you can take a walk, watch some social media posts, take a bath etc. which will charge your body and mind and put you in the top gear of learning. 7: Enjoy Learning Most people learn to score good marks in the examination or get a good job. Learning for them is a means to an end. I have always loved learning because I find that knowledge helps me develop a better understanding of the world and makes my life easier. in the words of Ralph Waldo Emerson — 'The mind, once stretched by a new idea, never returns to its original dimensions.' If you enjoy learning, you will not feel tired of learning since you will enjoy the process itself. Don’t consider learning as a job, a responsibility or a burden. Instead, think of learning as a process to acquire knowledge, which is a more valuable asset than wealth and power, that no one can gift you except yourself and no one can ever steal it from you. We become more enlightened and wiser human beings by learning, which gives us respect, honour, position, wealth, power and everything else that a human being desires in his or her life. Question: Is there really no such thing as a free lunch, or is that simply what people who get free lunches tell others?
Answer: When I was an IRS officer, the assessee would make different types of offers, when they meet you in the office, or at public functions. Many assesses also try to offer valuable gifts on special occasions like Diwali, New Year or Anniversaries. All these offers come with no terms and conditions and thus appear to be like free lunch. However, in reality, these people are not fools, but smart businessmen. The purpose of offering gifts to you is to develop an acquaintance with you, which can be exploited by them at the appropriate time. If you use their offers, they give it wide publicity to everyone (Saheb mere friend hai), particularly to your subordinates. As a result, the officers working under you can’t do their job fairly, and feel hesitant in booking cases against them. Morever, when you allow such people to come close to you, you also make yourself approachable, and vulnerable to further temptation and major corruption. Your reputation is gradually tarnished, if you develop acquaintance with the people with whom you have a professional relationship and you are expected to take against them if they commit some mischief. In modern times, we often get many things for free, and we happily use them without understanding the cost, we pay for them. We use social media platforms like Facebook, YouTube, and WhatsApp for free. Little do we realise that we are also shown many advertisements to lure us to buy things, which we may not need. Moreover, these companies collect data about us and sell them to commercial organisations, who keep chasing us to buy their products. Many car companies provide you with free test drives to develop an attachment to the vehicle they are selling. I can’t imagine a situation where you are offered something for free without any expectations. When political parties use government money to offer freebies to the poor people like free bus rides, education, rational, electricity, and medical care, they expect the beneficiaries to vote for them, and ignore their nepotism, inefficiency and corruption. Also remember that all freebies come from the taxpayer's money, which could have been used for the development of better infrastructure, industries, schools, hospitals etc. Even the benefits offered by your parents are not free, as they expect you to obey them and take care of them in their old age. Charles Petzold said it wisely, “Free lunches don't come cheap”. Hence, always be careful when someone offers you a free lunch because the cost you are likely to pay for the free lunch may be much higher than getting the lunch on your own money. You may not be paying money for your free lunch, but you may have to pay it with time, honour, moral degradation and compromise of your professionalism. , Source of picture: Google Images

Question: Why does it seem like the world is losing its morals?
Answer: Morality is concerned with what is right and wrong. A person is considered to be moral if he/she obeys the standard of behaviour that is considered good and right by most people. In simple words, morality means that you must obey public opinion, and sacrifice your wishes, aspirations, rights, liking, dreams and passion. Some good examples of such behaviours from Indian scriptures include In all cases, one thing is common. If you are superior in heirarchy, you can get away with any mistake, mischief, or misadventure, but, if you are inferior, you must pay the price for mistakes committed by your elders, and suffer the consequence, even if you are totally innocent. The moral values thus mean not only that you must subordinate yourself before society, but also before your parents and elders, and everyone above you in the social hierarchy. Hence, to be moral means, never to question the person in authority, whether it is a parent, husband, king, society, or God, and obey their orders faithfully. It means that the moral agent must not apply his mind to decide right and wrong for himself/herself and obey public opinion blindly. And for thousands of years, no one questioned whether the authority figure was right or wrong. It is good that the modern generation is now questioning the moral standards set in the ancient period when society was patriarchal, which subordinated women before men and wives before husbands, and not willing to accept a hierarchical social order which subordinated the children before parents, lower castes before upper castes, and pupils before the teacher. Accordingly, now women are not subordinate to men, husbands are not lords of the wives, and people of all castes, races and genders are working together in the common workplace with equal opportunities. Was such a type of working place ever possible in the past? When women are financially independent, educated and working together with men proving their value, they also seek equality and justice. Women today, are not things, subjects or property of the parents or the husband, and they won’t tolerate injustice and nonsense. Accordingly, now parents can’t force them to marry the man of their choice, and husbands can’t force them to remain at home. I don’t see anything immoral in giving equal rights and freedom to everyone. If the world seems to be losing its morals, it is because we are judging the morality of modern generation using the moral code of conduct of ancient periods which has now become totally outdated. Henry David Thoreau well said, “Do not be too moral. You may cheat yourself out of much life so. Aim above morality.” Instead of lamenting that the morality of the world is declining, understand morality rationality and you can see that we are actually progressing towards a better moral order and creating a fairer society. Question: What is the source of our moral values and behavior if God does not exist? Why are these values universal across cultures?
Answer: All moral values can be derived from the simple principle of the Golden Rule which denotes, “You should treat others the way you want to be treated yourself.” Sometimes, the Golden Rule is stated in a negative way, “Don't treat others in a way that you would not like to be treated.” For instance, we don’t want other people to lie to us, hate us, cheat us, harm us, or abuse us. Hence, lying, cheating, hate, violence, and abuse are considered immoral. We don’t want our spouse to be unfaithful to us, hence unfaithfulness and adultery are considered immoral. Similarly, if we apply the positive Golden Rule, The moral code of conduct has evolved over thousands of years to create better societies. When people followed the moral codes, they trusted each other and the societies became united and strong, and they could easily defeat those societies in which people had no morals and fought with each other. Hence, with evolution, the immoral societies perished while moral societies survived and thus moral values became part of human civilisation. God has nothing to do with morality, and the importance of God with respect to morality is only to create fear of God in the minds of common people to do the right thing, particularly when societies fail to punish immoral people. However, the fear of God can also be exploited to make the believers do horrible things like caste/religion based discrimination, terrorism and waging war against other communities. While most moral values like honesty, faithfulness, love, compassion etc. are universal, there are many moral values which are different across the world. The moral code of conduct based on religion is hardly universal and good for society because religion teaches believers to treat the members of their community differently as compared to those following other religions. Hence, religion based morality has been greatly reasonable for dividing the societies and creating hatred against one another. Steven Weinberg said very wisely, 'With or without religion, good people can behave well and bad people can do evil; but for good people to do evil - that takes religion.'

Question: What is a "common sense" concept you feel most people seem to be simply oblivious to?
Answer: I am a vegetarian by choice and conviction. My parents are also vegetarian, and hence meat was never cooked at home and I never tasted meat products. During my B Tech day, we stayed in the hostel and I had the opportunity to eat any non-vegetarian food, but by then, I had developed the conviction that meat eating is bad, and hence I never felt tempted by meat products and never consumed them. While my daughters are vegetarians, their spouses are non-vegetarians. Almost everyone in the family of my in-laws is non-vegetarian, and so are the spouses of my siblings. Today, while surfing on Facebook, I came across the following quote. This quote resonates with my core belief, due to which, I resisted eating meat despite opportunity and financial resources. Now, if I share this quote on my family WhatsApp group, what will happen? My post is sure to offend all meat eaters in my family, even if they don't retaliate against my post due to my age and respect. However, if I keep sharing such posts without giving due thought to how it is going to affect others, I will soon lose their love and respect forever simply for speaking my mind. Albert Einstein said it wisely, "Common sense is a collection of prejudices acquired by the age of eighteen." Let us understand that there can be many perspectives of the same reality, and what looks right to us, may not look correct to others, just as we don’t accept their views. The common sense is to understand that our habits are beliefs are intimately connected. While we may not know the beliefs of a person as no one can read the minds of others, we can identify beliefs from their habits. Hence, if you love a person, you must also respect his/her beliefs and sentiments and not post anything on a family WhatsApp group, which may offend your loved ones. A few years ago, in our family WhatsApp group, there used to be many political and religious posts, which were followed by heated discussions, where some members would be very vocal in their views while others would silently read the post. So, much so that it started affecting the personal relationships between the family members. I had to literally fight a battle to stop political and religious posts on our family groups. Thankfully, such posts have stopped now for several years and now there is peace and harmony in the family groups. It is important to understand that if you fall ill or face some trouble, you can’t expect Modi, Yogi or Rahul Gandhi to come to your help, and only your family and friends will come to help you. Let us be guided by the beautiful quote of Voltaire — 'Everything you say should be true, but not everything true should be said.' How stupid it is to spoil your relationships for political and religious views. Unfortunately, most people lack the common sense to understand these simple rules of life, which makes them isolated and even discarded by their loved ones. I don’t understand why so many people lack the common sense to understand this simple truth that you don’t have all the knowledge of the world, and you must respect, or at least tolerate divergent views and opinions to connect and bond with people.

Question: What is the significance of the Supreme Court order on the electoral bond?
Answer: The electoral bond system was brought by the Modi Government in 2017, which allowed individuals and companies to donate money to political parties anonymously and without any limits. It allowed a person or company can buy electoral bonds from the State Bank of India and donate them to a political party of their choice. Today, the Supreme Court of India pronounced its judgement on petitions challenging the electoral bonds scheme, concluding that it is violative of Article 19(1)(a) and unconstitutional. The main highlights of the judgements are as follows. Accordingly, the SC directed that the issuing banks stop issuing electoral bonds and directed the State Bank of India shall submit details of bonds purchased since the apex court’s interim order of April 12, 2019, including the date of encashment and denomination, to the Election Commission by March 6, 2024, and that the electoral body should share this information on its website. Further, the Chief Justice of India, in his verdict, said that financial contributions to political parties are made for two parties, either for support to a political party, or contribution may be a way of quid pro quo,[1] i.e. provided as a bribe to the party in power for a benefit accorded to it. BJP has been the largest beneficiary of the electoral bonds (54% of the total receipt in FY 22). The income in FY 2023 is shown in the following chart. [2] According to disclosures by political parties, the BJP received ₹ 5,270 crore out of a total of ₹ 9,208 crore or 57 per cent of all total electoral bonds sold till 2022. The main opposition Congress party came a distant second, receiving ₹ 964 crore or 10 per cent in the same period, while West Bengal's ruling Trinamool Congress got ₹ 767 crore or 8 per cent of all electoral bonds.[3] The huge money that the BJP gets through these bonds clearly gives them an edge during the elections as compared to other political parties. We can only hope that the judgement of the Supreme Court shall be observed the SBI shall disclose the list to the Election Commission, and the public can know if there are any special benefits given by the government to the donating parties. The judgment of the Supreme Court will certainly improve (if implemented) the transparency and accountability in the electoral processes in India. However, it is unlikely that the Modi Government will take the adverse judgement of the Supreme Court lying down. Most likely, they will bring an ordinance to overturn the Supreme Court judgement because they know their supporters hardly bother about the legality and constitutionality of their actions. It is good that at least one institution in India (the Supreme Court) has the courage to protect the constitution, at least of now, and show the mirror to the Government. Question: Is there more evil than good or does it just stick out more?
Answer: Humans have a very strange method of calculating evil in men. Unfortunately, the second method is used in the world to calculate the evilness of a person. If you do a single evil act, you will be termed as evil, even if you have done a million good acts. Now, is it possible that a person has never committed a single act of evil in his entire life? There is a famous story in the Bible (John 8: 1–11) that explains that the way, the world defines evil, there are no good men left in the world. As Jesus was speaking, the teachers of religious law and the Pharisees brought a woman who had been caught in the act of adultery. They put her in front of the crowd. “Teacher,” they said to Jesus, “this woman was caught in the act of adultery. The law of Moses says to stone her. What do you say?” They were trying to trap him into saying something they could use against him, but Jesus stooped down and wrote in the dust with his finger. They kept demanding an answer, so he stood up again and said, “All right, but let the one who has never sinned throw the first stone!” Then he stooped down again and wrote in the dust. When the accusers heard this, they slipped away one by one, beginning with the oldest, until only Jesus was left in the middle of the crowd with the woman. Then Jesus stood up again and said to the woman, “Where are your accusers? Didn’t even one of them condemn you?” “No, Lord,” she said. And Jesus said, “Neither do I. Go and sin no more.” Since a good man is termed as a sinner or an evil person by a single bad act, and the world does not allow him to become good again, whatever good he does thereafter, the world has become full of evil and we find no good person around. In reality, the world is full of good people and almost every human being does more good than evil. However, due to our faulty methodology to calculate evil wherein we ignore all goodness for a single evil, we can’t see goodness in the world. Evil is like an illness that makes a healthy person sick for a shortwhile. The goal of the doctor is to treat the patient to make him healthy again rather than condemning him forever for falling ill. A popular adage says, “Hate the sin, love the sinner.” A good person does not become evil by a single act of evil. If we rationally add the good and evil acts of the people, we will find the world full of good people since rarely does a person’s evil exceed his goodness in life. Source of picture: Google Images

Question: What is wrong with being in a live-in relationship in India?
Answer: India is a complex country, which can be best represented by the following picture. This is a picture of 1981, when Indian space scientists were gearing up for the launch of its first communication satellite APPLE from the Guiana Space Centre in France, they had loaded the satellite onto a bullock cart. Just like, in India, bullock ca[1]rd and rocket science exist together, Indians also follow the culture that existed several thousand years ago in the Vedic period as well as the latest culture of 21st century in the most developed country in the world. Yesterday was Mauni Amavasya, and more than 2 crore (20 million) pilgrims took holy dip at Sangam, in sangam at Prayagraj. [2] Most of these people don’t even know the meaning of a live-in relationship and for them, marriage is a sacred ceremony which can’t be broken in this life. Even today, almost 50% of the Indian population is in villages and they can’t even imagine an unmarried boy and girl living together in the same house as a couple. For them sex is permitted only between the husband and wife and anything else is immoral. Even among those, who have migrated to cities in last couple of decades ago, largely share the same traditional Indian values and treat marriage a sacred institution, and sex before marriage immoral. However, within India, there is also a small segment which is as Western in thought as any European or American country. They feel free to drink and dance at the party and don’t hesitate to engage in premarital or extramarital sex, similar to their Western counterparts. [3] Hence, the rightness or wrongness of a live-in relaship depends, on which class of Indian society you belong to. A few years ago, a boy well-known to me, who came from a middle-class background from a small town, lived in with his girlfriend. However, after a couple of months, when the girl wanted to marry him, he refused because his parents refused permission to marry the girl due to caste and status differences. The boy was also not very fond of the girl and did not wish to marry her. The girl refused to let the matter go and filed a complaint of sexual harassment/rape with the police and claimed that he induced her to have sex with the promise to marry. She lamented that no one is going to marry her after knowing that she was living-in with him. The police came quick to arrest him, but he fled. Finally, on the advice of his well-wishers and lawyers, he agreed to marry her. In such cases in India, the boy is generally arrested, though in many cases, the boy gets acquitted after spending years in Jail and losing all his reputation. The woman also loses her reputation, as most people consider her characterless and very few boys would be willing to marry her after the breakup. You may find numerous such news items almost on a daily basis in India. Even if you are rich and belong to the highest class of Indian society, don’t forget that most of the police officials and judges belong to the middle class and still carry the old Indian values where marriage is treated as a sacred ceremony and sex before marriage is considered immoral. Hence, if your live-in partner (girl) makes an allegation of rape against you, most likely you may go to jail and spend several months, if not years in jail. However, if both boys and girls are westernised, open-minded and have a liberal outlook on sex outside marriage, then live-in relationships may be fine and acceptable by the most elite class of society. While live-in may be acceptable in metro cities, it is still a taboo in most parts of India. Hence, be careful before choosing a live-in relationship in India based on your outlook on life and your cultural background.

Question: Why are some people evil? Are they born that way or does life make them evil?
Answer: In 1960, the psychologist Walter Mischel, then a professor at Stanford University, and his team conducted a series of studies. In these studies, children (16 boys and 16 girls, aged between 4–6 years) were offered a choice between In follow-up studies, the researchers found that children who were able to wait longer for the larger rewards tended to have better life outcomes, as measured by SAT scores, educational attainment, body mass index (BMI), and other life measures. This experiment proves that if we can resist instant gratification, we can achieve great success in life in every field. This experiment also established that even children as young as 4 to 6 years have different abilities to resist the temptation of instant pleasure.[1] In my opinion, the root cause of all evil is our inability to resist the temptation. We all face numerous types of temptations in our lives. People become evil due to their inability to resist the temptation of wealth, power, fame, or sexual pleasure. According to Christian tradition, there are seven deadly sins, and all happen due to our inability of resist temptation We all live in the same world and face the same temptations in our lives. Those who resist temptations become great human beings, while those who can’t resist temptation become evil. We can resist temptation by developing our rational minds and inculcating high moral values by constantly resisting temptation. in the words of Ralph Waldo Emerson, “We gain the strength of the temptation we resist”. Finally, whether people are born evil or life makes them evil? I think it is a combination of both. The Stanford marshmallow experiments reveal that the ability to resist temptation is present from an early age, and hence part of the tendency to do evil is inborn. It is common to find that even when two siblings are brought up in the same family, one may become good and one evil. However, a good-natured person can become evil when he is treated badly and unfairly by the world, while and bad-natured person can become good if he lives in the company of good people. Hence, evil is partly a product of nature as well as nurture. However, it is always possible for even the evilest person to become good with great effort, and even the best person to fall prey to evil, if he becomes careless about his or her conduct. Oscar Wilde said it aptly, 'Every saint has a past, and every sinner has a future.' Source of picture: Google Images

Question: Do people like things because they're good at it or that since they like something, they become good at it?
Answer: Every year, almost a million young Indians appear for the civil services examination for less than a thousand seats. They all like to become top civil servants in India, but 99.9% fail to make it into civil service because they are not good enough to be selected for the civil services examination. Even the thousand candidates who get selected through this rigorous examination, hardly 10% turn out to be good civil servants. We like a thing that fulfils our desires and it has nothing to do with our being good at it. For instance, most people like to become top civil servants in India due to its glamorous components like power, perks (legal and illegal), social recognition and security of the job. People like things which fulfil their desires without ever assessing whether they are good at it. For example, Hence, it is evident that the first part of question i.e. the statement “People like things because they are good at it” is incorrect. Let us now examine the second part of the question: When people like something, they become good at it. No one is born good at anything at birth. We have to work hard to develop the knowledge and skills to become good at it. Malcolm Gladwell in his book“Outliers: The Story of Success” repeatedly refers to the “10,000-hour rule,” asserting that the key to achieving true expertise in any skill is simply a matter of practising, albeit in the correct way, for at least 10,000 hours.[1] Now, can you spend 10,000 hours of your life acquiring something unless you like doing the job? Since I joined Quora in December 2014, I have written more than 5600 answers, which must have consumed almost 10,000 hours of my time in writing answers and dealing with the comments of the readers. I have made practically no money by spending more than 10,000 hours of my life on Quora. Similarly, I have spent even more time writing my nine books and earned hardly any income from it. So, why did I spend tens of thousands of time writing with no tangible benefit? The simple reason for writing is that I like (more appropriately, I love) writing. Only when you like or love something, you can do the thing naturally without any end goal because the process itself provides you immense satisfaction. Gradually, you become good at what you like, which makes you like it even more. As a result, you not only become good at doing the things you like, but you also enjoy tremndous happiness doing something you love to do, and achieve success in your chosen field. Albert Schweitzer wisely said, “Success is not the key to happiness. Happiness is the key to success. If you love what you are doing, you will be successful.” Hence, the most important requirement for living a great life is to identify what you like, not as a means to achieve something else, but due to your liking for the thing itself, and then work hard to become good at it, and excellence shall follow naturally.
