Question: Is India ready for a uniform civil code? What would be the benefits in eliminating religious personal laws? Are the concerns against it justified?
Answer: The recent statement of Indian Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi that India needed a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) as the country could not run with the dual system of “separate laws for separate communities”, has fuelled speculation for the implementation of Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in India soon. UCC has been in the manifesto of the BJP for a long time and with Modi Government commanding a majority in Parliament, there is a high possibility of UCC law being passed soon. The Uniform Civil Code means that the same law shall be applicable to all uniformly in matters of - Marriage, divorce, maintenance, inheritance, adoption and succession of property, irrespective of religion. The term, ‘Uniform Civil Code’ is explicitly mentioned in Article 44 of the Indian Constitution, which says “The State shall endeavor to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India.” In my opinion, UCC is good for the country as it will be in the spirit of secular India where people shall be given equal status irrespective of their religion. Objections against UCC Since UCC shall be dealing with issues like marriage, divorce, maintenance etc, which have been traditionally decided on the basis of religion, the detractors would contend that it will rob the nation of its religious diversity and violate the fundamental right to practise religion enshrined in Article 25 and Article 29 of the Constitution. They argue that UCC is a directive principle which can’t override the fundamental rights enshrined in the Constitution. Article 25 provides the freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion, while Article 29 provides that all sections of the citizens having a distinct language, script or culture of their own shall have the right to conserve the same. However, I believe that many cultures and traditions have outdated and must be discarded as soon as possible to create a modern society. For example, there is no provision for divorce and property inheritance by daughters in the Hindu religion. However, Indian laws have been implemented to provide these rights to Hindu women. In Islam, there is a provision that men can marry up to four women. Similarly, divorce provisions are much easier in Islam, and even triple talaq is permitted. Further, under Muslim personal law, maintenance was to be paid only till the period of iddat. (three lunar months-roughly 90 days ).[1] Way Ahead I don’t think that any right-minded person would support the right of a man to have four wives. The very concept appears repugnant to me, which denies dignity to women in the modern world. I also believe that women of all religions must be equally protected from arbitrary divorce and given the same compensation which can ensure them a dignified life. Surely, there will be opposition to the UCC by some people and political parties to influence their vote bank. Yet, the opponents of UCC would be in small numbers in India and those who oppose UCC may pay a heavy price for opposing this progressive move by Government. However, the drafting of UCC must be done very carefully incorporating the best practices of all religions so that no religion feels discriminated against or privileged.

Question: Is life unfair for everybody or just for some people?
Answer: On my Facebook feeds, I often get videos of wildlife. The most common videos are of lions chasing other wild animals, catching them and then devouring them. How do you feel while watching the videos? Our natural reaction is that life is very unfair to the poor animals which are killed by the mighty tiger/lion. If we would have been there on the spot, we would perhaps like to save the life of the poor animals to create a just world. But do you think that life is fair to the tiger? Christopher McDougall writes in his book Born to Run, “Every morning in Africa, a gazelle wakes up, it knows it must outrun the fastest lion or it will be killed. Every morning in Africa, a lion wakes up. It knows it must run faster than the slowest gazelle, or it will starve. It doesn't matter whether you're the lion or a gazelle-when the sun comes up, you'd better be running.” Imagine the fate of a lion or tiger, which can’t eat grass or other fruits like a deer for survival, but has to live only on the flesh of other animals. Nature has not given them any option to these poor creatures to live a nonviolent life. When they fall sick or get old, they die of hunger because they can’t chase other animals. The concept of justice, fairness, equality etc, are not natural, but purely a human creation. In the natural world, there is inequality in the human kingdom as in the wild. Some people are beautiful, while others are ugly, some are intelligent while others are unintelligent, some are powerful, others are weak, some are born rich, while others are born poor. Even within the same family, males and females are not equal in terms of physical strength, intelligence, beauty, responsibilities etc. How fair it is that females are physically weaker, and have to suffer labour pain, while men can enjoy their life without undergoing such pain for procreation? However, when you look at the totality of things, you will find that with every advantage comes some additional responsibility which neutralises the advantage. Let’s go through the following Aesop’s Fable. A Horse and an Ass were travelling together, the Horse prancing along in its fine trappings, the Ass carrying with difficulty the heavy weight in its panniers. “I wish I were you,” sighed the Ass; “nothing to do and well fed, and all that fine harness upon you.” The next day, however, there was a great battle, and the Horse was wounded to death in the final charge of the day. His friend, the Ass, happened to pass by shortly afterwards and found him on the point of death. “I was wrong,” said the Ass: “Better humble security than gilded danger.”[1] Life is what it is. If you ignore the advantages you have and consider only the shortcoming, life is unfair to you. However, if you learn to take a holistic view, and focus on what you have, instead of what you don’t have, you will find sufficient reason to be grateful and feel happy about the justice of life. Question: Do you agree that sometimes good people do bad things? If so, why?
Answer: In Beyond Good And Evil Nietzsche argues that the concepts of good and evil are culturally constructed rather than inherently "true". Accordingly, different cultures develop different moral laws in order to maintain social order. For example, for a Jain, and for many Hindus, eating meat would be very bad as it involves killing a life. However, for a Muslim, killing animals on certain occasions may be a religious duty and is considered to be good. Billions of meat eaters around the world would not consider meat eating as bad. Similarly, drinking alcohol would be a sin for Muslims, but acceptable for Christians. In fact, the first miracle that Jesus Christ performed was to convert water to alcohol. For billions of people around the world, alcohol is a drink of celebration and festivity. Almost everything can be viewed as good and evil by different people depending upon their outlook. Hence, one thing is certain that no person can be good in the eyes of every person, nor can any person be bad for everyone. Even a person who is treated as a criminal and considered bad by the society may actually be a good person for his family member and friend. You perhaps know the people in the picture. On the left side, we have Mahatma Gandhi, who is considered to be a saint and one of the greatest leaders of the 20th century and respected all over the world. On the right side is Nathuram Godse, who killed Gandhi ji. While most people may consider Gandhi as good, and Godse as evil, there are also millions of people who consider Godse as good and Gandhi as bad. However, there are some actions which are universally considered good or bad. For instance, most people would agree that lying, cheating, murder, rape, infidelity, theft, corruption etc. are bad while truthfulness, honesty, love and compassion, faithfulness, charity and integrity are good. No person is born good or bad. We become good or bad depending on our actions. According to Aristotle, “Excellence is an art won by training and habituation. We do not act rightly because we have virtue or excellence but we rather have those because we have acted rightly. We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act but is a habit.” In my life, I have not come across any person who has never done anything bad, or always done only bad things in life. We all are good at times, while bad at other times. However, the proportion of good and bad may be different in different people. Hence, we can compare goodness and evilness only on a relative scale. Some people are better than others, but no person is absolutely good or absolutely bad. So, we must try to do as much good things as possible, but not be ashamed of ourselves, if we sometimes commit bad things as well. Let us remember, “To err is human, and to forgive is divine”. It is thus important not only to commit as few errors as we can but also to have the heart to forgive those who sometimes err and give them the opportunity to become good again. No one can be good in the eyes of everyone, perhaps not even God. Source of picture: Google Images

Question: Why is life so unfair to good people?
Answer: One of my relatives had always followed good habits in life. He never drank or smoked and ate moderately. He used to get up early in the morning, and do pranayama and yoga for almost an hour. Then he used to take a walk for almost an hour. We used to give his example for healthy living. Around four years ago, he was diagnosed with lung cancer in the last state and died within a month at the age of 70 years. On the other side, I know a couple of people, who are regular smokers and drinkers, but they did not get lung cancer and living a healthy life even at 80 years. Should I conclude from this incident that life is unfair to nonsmokers, as they die due to cancer while smokers live full life? If we wish to understand reality, we must have an analytical mind and learn to think critically. So let’s get our facts right. According to the Center for Disease Prevention and Control (CDC), cigarette smoking is the number one risk factor for lung cancer. In the United States, cigarette smoking is linked to about 80% to 90% of lung cancer deaths. Using other tobacco products such as cigars or pipes also increases the risk of lung cancer.[1] This research does not say that all smokers will get lung cancer and nonsmokers would not be affected by cancer. However, the study clearly points out that your chances of getting lung cancer would be multiplied by several times if you smoke. Let us now come to the question of whether or not life is unfair to good people. It is true that some good people suffer great problems in life while some bad people continue to enjoy their lives despite all evil acts. However, if we collect data on good and evil people, we will find that bad people are many times more likely to suffer problems than good people. Let's take the case of Atique Ahmed, the dreaded gangster of yesteryears. He is in jail for several years and his entire family is either arrested or absconding. Yesterday, his son was killed in a police encounter. Now according to the media reports, such was the terror of gangster-turned-politician Atique Ahmed that in 2012 as many as 10 judges of Allahabad High Court had recused themselves from hearing his bail plea. Ahmed was planning to fight assembly polls from Allahabad West constituency as a candidate of Apna Dal. Today, nearly a decade later, 61-year-old Ahmed reportedly fainted and cried when he heard the news of Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force killing his son Asad in an encounter in Jhansi.[2] How many good people suffer this type of fate? Atique is not an exception, as there are hundreds of millions of people languishing in prison for crime, corruption, or fraud all over the world, while good people going to prison and losing the respect of society is rarest of rare. Even when they are send to prison ( Like Gandhi or Nelson Mandela), or killed (Bhagat Singh, Lincoln), their honour is enhanced and they are treated as heroes. It is true that some good people also suffer in the world, but like my relative who died of cancer, their numbers are much lower than those who suffer because of their evil deeds. Life is thus not unfair to good people but rewards good people to lead a better life in the world. So, if you intend to become a bad person, be ready to pay the price for your evil deeds, as and when your karma catches you. Source of picture: Google Images

Question: Why do some people not follow any religion?
Answer: Religion is said to be the opium of the masses because the first thing religions do is to make your mind incapable of any logical and rational thinking. Hence, every religion tempers your mind by first telling you some cock and bull story, which no sane person would ever believe. However, if you still happen to believe in such an absurd story, it means that your mind is now ripe for implanting any type of thoughts because you have stopped trusting your mind to know the truth. You are now ready to be a believer, who can now accept anything and everything as true by simply connecting such statements with God. When you by chance find any fallacy in the religion, there is another fallacy ready to defend the earlier ones. However, if at any time in your life, you are awaked from your deep slumber of ignorance, you will realise that religions are myths, which are believed so widely that they have become true in the eyes of the believers while remaining a fallacy for the rest of mankind, including the believers of other religion. If you don’t trust me, read the posts on any social media platforms where the followers of different religions fight like dogs to prove that their religion is right and others are wrong. Let’s take the example of the creation of the universe in 7 days as described in Bible (Genesis). According to Bible, on the sixth day, God created animals that live on the land and finally humans, made in the image of God were created. And by day seven - God finished his work of creation and rested, making the seventh day a special holy day.[1] However, according to Hinduism, the universe was created in a totally different manner. In Garuda Purana, there was nothing in the universe except Brahman. The universe became an expanse of water, and in that, Vishnu was born in the golden egg. He created Brahma with four faces. Brahma then created the devas, asuras, pitris and manushas, and others. [2] If all religions are the words of God, how can any of them be wrong? And if none of them is wrong, who is right? I don’t understand how a person with a logical mind can accept such theories of creation ignoring the theory of evolution, with no evidence in support of the claim. Similarly, according to the Gospel of John, Jesus transformed water into wine at a wedding in Cana. [3]You must be totally ignorant of the laws of science to believe that water can be converted into wine. Similarly, in Hindu mythologies, you can find numerous instances which are simply impossible, like Lord Hanuman eating the sun or flying 2000 kilometres with a mountain. There are also numerous instances in almost every religion where the prophet, Avatar or son of God has made the dead people alive, which may be a great wish for all humans, but not possible as against the law of nature. Yet billions beleive in such miracles without evidence. As a matter of fact, they believe in their Gods precisely because they expect God to break the natural laws for them and perform miracles according to their desires. Almost all major religions are thousands of years old and they were based on the knowledge of humankind that existed at that time. In those days, perhaps the God hypothesis was necessary to fill the gap and explain the working of the world in coherent ways. However, humans have acquired hundreds of times more knowledge since then and developed much better theories based on scientific studies to explain the working of the world. When people develop confidence in their own minds and reason, they lose faith in religion and refuse to blindly follow any religion. Instead, they apply their minds and choose their actions based on their best judgements and the correct knowledge of the world.

Question: What is holding back India's progress?
Answer: There is interesting news today published in all leading newspapers of India. The study contradicts existing beliefs about the antibacterial properties of cow urine and highlights that it cannot be recommended for human consumption.[1] I did not find anything surprising in the research because I know that if there be an iota of truth in the medical utility of cow urine, scientists worldwide would have been using cow urine for treating various diseases. However, I am very sure that millions of Indians, including highly educated ones, would dismiss such research, and continue to believe that cow urine is nothing less than a miraculous medicine. People believe in the miraculous properties of cow urine because according to Ayurveda, Gomutra (cow urine) can cure leprosy, fevers, peptic ulcers, liver ailments, kidney disorders, asthma, certain allergies, psoriasis, anaemia and even cancer.[2] Since something is written in the holy book of Ayurveda, how can it be wrong? Many top Indian leaders keep advocating the use of cow urine for cure of any ailment, including COvid-19 virus. For example, some time ago, West Bengal BJP president Dilip Ghosh advocated the use of “cow-urine” to boost immunity in the fight against COVID-19. [3] Similarly, BJP MP Pragya Thakur claimed that cow urine can cure lung infection caused by Coronavirus, adding she is protected from the virus as she takes cow urine every day. She told a party gathering sometime ago, “If we have desi gau mutra (urine from an indigenous cow)[how nationalistic!] every day then it cures lung infection from Covid. I am in deep pain but I take cow urine every day. So, now I don’t have to take any medicine against corona and I don't have corona.”[4] The Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan even claimed: “cows, cow-dung and its urine can help strengthen the economy of the state and entire nation if a proper system is put in place”. The most unfortunate thing about most Indians is that they have little faith in scientific study and more faith in the words of their leaders (religious and political) and the ancient scriptures. There are millions of such myths, which are totally false and unscientific, and still, hundreds of millions Indians believe in such lies. Unless Indians learn to think rationally, develop a scientific temper, and stop believing in mythologies, India can never become a happy, developed and prosperous nation.

Question: Is it true that Hanuman is still alive, in this age & time?

Do not believe in anything merely on the authority of your teachers and elders. Do not believe in traditions because they have been handed down for many generations. But after observation and analysis, when you find that anything agrees with reason and is conducive to the good and benefit of one and all, then accept it and live up to it.”[3] The choice to accept something as true is yours because the mind is yours and the life is yours. It would be wise to remember the words of George Bernard Shaw, 'Beware of false knowledge; it is more dangerous than ignorance.'

The question which is invariably asked is if I am satisfied with their services, and if have made any payment to their technician. Thereafter, they always send me a feedback form where I have to rate their services, generally from 1–10. I remember an incident that happened around a year ago, when my Tata play Fiber service got some issues because the fibre was cut somewhere. The local technician came and tried to fix the problem for several hours, but could not do it. However, in the end, he closed the complaint, falsely indicating that the problem was resolved. The next day, I got a feedback call. I told them the truth and said that the technician has falsely reported that the problem was resolved and that the internet connection is still not working. As a result, the technician was fired badly, and penalised. The next day, the technician came and he was almost in tears. I told him that he must not have reported falsely. He begged that if there is any issue in future, please call me directly and I will fix the issue quickly. After that incident, my internet connection ran smoothly. If the government at the centre and state level develop a feedback system, give a call to citizens on a random basis, and send a feedback form to every citizen after they have availed of any government service, they can quickly know about the corrupt officer. Once you have got feedback from the citizens, about the corruption of an officer, and know the modus Operandi, the anti-corruption agency can catch the officer red-handed with the help of citizens. Moreover, the government will have an authentic database about the integrity and efficiency of all officers in the department, which can be used by the government to reward, punishments and decide postings to the officers. Government must also provide a helpline number, where citizens can report their complaints anonymously.
